## OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-05: WAIT — the 5796 -> e369 dependency is real

The blocking chain was surfaced to the operator, including the observation that 5796 is titled
"follow-on to e369" yet is modelled as a hard `depends_on`, which prevents any DC-hardening
work starting until every e369 bug closes. The operator considered re-modelling it to
`relates_to` and chose NOT to: the dependency is intended.

So this ticket waits. e369's sole remaining unclosed child is bug 8390-32f7-e4b8-48a1, actively
held by another session. When it closes, e369 closes, 5796 becomes claimable, and this ticket
resumes.

Nothing here is lost. The hard part is DONE and recorded on this ticket: the port is provably
dead, confirmed by BOTH a semantic search and a string grep, with the dynamic-load path chased
separately (two docstrings claiming `inbound_probe.py` is "loaded by filename elsewhere" are
STALE — nothing loads it). Two false positives are ruled out and recorded: `probe_remote_branch`
in `_commands/_init_probe.py` is unrelated, and the OUTBOUND probe chain is live and must not
be touched. The plan carries a PASS attestation and `file_impact` over 26 files.

To resume: `review-plan 5796` -> `claim f020` -> execute the deletion as the description
specifies.
